gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noto-sans-linear: Chunky, hand-cut and cheerful, Balsamiq Sans leads with strokes that never thin out. Noto Sans Linear A follows in a clean sans whose gaping c keeps a long stretch of text open and legible.
Noto Sans Linear B moves smoothly around every bend, modern and unfussy in its sans manner. And Balsamiq Sans earns its keep when it goes big and brief, drawing each letter with one constant line.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noto-sans-manich: Strokes with no swelling and no thinning give Balsamiq Sans its marker-pen bluntness. Noto Sans Manichaean, a modern plain sans with open-mouthed e crossbars, is what makes that bluntness easy to live with.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noto-sans-mongol:
Balsamiq Sans draws everything with one stubborn stroke width.

Noto Sans Mongolian, a sans-serif with outward-flaring terminals, supplies the lighter, more modern texture underneath, so the page has a loud voice and a quieter one.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noto-sans-new-ta: Noto Sans New Tai Lue shapes its round letters so they look cupped rather than clenched, modern and plain. Balsamiq Sans earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noto-sans-nko: Modern and see-through, Noto Sans NKo keeps its c openings wide enough to look straight through. Balsamiq Sans is best at loud, heavy-lined display, while Noto Sans NKo is best at the sans-serif quiet that follows.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noto-sans-old-so: Approachable is the mood in both, though in different volumes: Balsamiq Sans is thick-lined and expressive, drawn like a thread of ink. And Noto Sans Old South Arabian keeps its sans curves ending before they turn inward, which lets the heading do the shouting.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-noto-sans-shavia: Noto Sans Shavian has rope-loose curves that never knot at their ends, clean and contemporary in a sans-serif way. Balsamiq Sans then adds a thread-like, bold heading above it.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-ojuju: Ojuju reads like a sans-serif drawn with lightly flexed spring wire, approachable, with wide s curves barely curled in. Shrink Balsamiq Sans and its brushy single-stroke look gets lost.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-overpass: Overpass reads modern and sturdy, with strokes that never mix bold-looking and light-looking in one word. Balsamiq Sans is best at brash, constant-width headings, while Overpass is best at the plain sans work of carrying the text.
